entries.title: Love and weddings
entries.answer: Two folk who grow as fond of each other as folk get pledge themselves, and the next evening the town holds the wedding: the couple at the heart, the town in a ring, the bell, vows, cheers and dancing. They move into the better of their two houses. Players don't marry folk, but you can be a godparent to their children.
tips: Ask 'Family & friends' (About tab) or 'Gossip' to hear who's together and who's sweet on whom.
A widow or widower may love and marry again.

entries.title: Children and godparents
entries.answer: A child is born to a fed couple in work when there's room and food put by. For three days it plays (tag, trailing its parents, exploring), goes to school, then grows up and takes a trade. A friend of the town can ask a child 'Be godparent': it thinks the world of you, and its parents the better of you.
controls: [Right-click] a child → About → Home & pet → Be godparent
tips: Ask a child about itself and it says what it'll be when it grows up.
A child born into a full house gets a bed its parents buy at the shop.

entries.title: Households, homes and beds
entries.answer: Every folk belongs to a household (itself, its partner, their children) with a house of its own, first let by the council and later saved up for and bought. Grown children move out when a house is free; a folk without a bed lodges in a spare one; the builders put up houses while anyone waits.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → About → Home & pet → Your home?
tips: A house shows who lives in it: its trade's things and luxuries (rugs, paintings, quilts), furnished out of ten.

entries.title: Pets: dogs and cats
q: how do i get a pet
entries.answer: Households keep dogs and cats with a bowl by the hearth, a dog bed or cat basket, and a collar in the pet's colour. Right-click a household's pet with a Pet Treat to befriend it (two treats and it's your friend); right-click a stray with a treat to adopt it; or buy a pup or kitten from a litter (3 coins) by holding coins and right-clicking it.
controls: [Right-click] a pet with a Pet Treat
[Right-click] a folk → About → Home & pet → Your pet?
tips: Recipes: Pet Treat (2 wheat and a meat or fish, makes 4), Pet Bowl (planks, a bowl, planks; or 5 bricks for 2), Dog Bed (wool in 5 planks), Cat Basket (wool in 5 sticks), Pet Collar (string, leather, string; dye it like leather armour).
Place a bowl or bed in a folk's house and the household uses it.

entries.title: Fashion and clothes
q: can i give clothes to villagers
entries.answer: Over its trade's clothes a folk wears what it bought, was given or won: a long coat, leather jacket, shawl or waistcoat, a felt hat, flat cap or top hat off work, a scarf, a brooch, a rosette. Fashions sweep through: a colour and a garment set by those the town looks up to, made by the tailor, and soon most of the town wears it.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → More chat → Fashion?
tips: Hand a folk a garment (Give) and it puts it on there and then.
Every garment but the brooch can be dyed in a crafting grid, like leather armour.

entries.title: Health, healers and the infirmary
entries.answer: Folk catch colds out in the rain or worked to the bone; a cold halves their pace for a day or two and never kills. A Stone Age town of twenty builds an infirmary; its healer sees to the sick. Hurt yourself? Ask the healer 'See to me' for a remedy and a fee.
controls: [Right-click] the healer → Trade → Services → See to me
tips: Bandages (2 paper and a string, or a wool and 2 string, make 3) are the watch's and cave team's kit.
Herbal tea (sweet berries or a small flower, sugar, a water bottle) is a cup for a cold.

entries.title: Old age, deaths and vigils
entries.answer: Folk grow old and die in time (and sometimes in raids or wars). The evening after a death the town gathers quietly at the heart for a vigil, and those close grieve for a while. The chronicle remembers everyone.
tips: Old folk with poor eyes are delighted by Spectacles.

entries.title: School, library and learning
entries.answer: Children go to school each morning (a schoolteacher, desks, a blackboard; Slate and Chalk helps them learn a quarter faster). The town library keeps a catalogue of real books by its writers and lends them; the store buys written books for it.

entries.title: The museum
entries.answer: The museum shows the town's rare finds (gems, discs, templates, a nether star...) and the first of each invention's working model; what it shows counts toward the town's renown. The store buys a kind of find it hasn't got.

entries.title: Eating out: café, tavern, restaurant, inn
q: how do i eat at the restaurant
entries.answer: Sit at a table in the café, tavern or restaurant (right-click a chair or the cloth, or a waiter) and the order screen opens: pick dishes from the card, choose at the table, to take away or brought to you anywhere in town, and Order. The waiter brings it on a plate as a place setting: right-click to eat a bite. At a tavern ask the barkeep for a pint or a round; at an inn, a room for the night.
controls: [Right-click] a chair or table cloth → order screen
Barkeep → Trade → Shop → A pint · Buy a round · Bottles back
Innkeeper → A room for the night
tips: A plate and cup of your own (bricks and clay) can be set on a table too.
Each town has a local dish, marked on the card.

entries.title: Culture: banner, customs, arms
entries.answer: Each town has its own culture: a banner and arms (granted a charge such as a fish, pick or sheaf), a motto, customs, a local dish, music, a theatre and plaques. The village board flies its banner; citizens are given it. The Culture page shows it all.

entries.title: Seasons, weather, fire and drought
entries.answer: The year turns through seasons that change what's grown, eaten and worn, with festivals in each. Towns face fires, floods and droughts too: the folk fight fires with buckets and rain barrels, and the News page records it.
